text:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: v2.14.0 -> edge-eu-west1, fraction=5%, id=deploy-20260312-1145. kickoff 09:12 UTC.

incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> INC12345: production: embed-gen 5xx surge (service: inference-embed). threshold: 15m 5xx rate > 2% on canary. paging oncall.

Olivia (oncall): ack INC12345, taking it. pinging SRE/eng.

Sam (sre): on it. pulling traces now — seeing p95 latency spike and ~3.8% 5xx from the canary subset. related to `embed-gen` backend. trace id samples: rK9Q2, rK9Q3.

Anna (eng): heads up — v2.14.0 enabled a new quant kernel selection path that only runs for long sequences, but we enabled a fallback for short sequences. wondering if canary traffic distribution pushed some long inputs through.

Carter (support): CS already triaged ~12 support hits, 3 customers reporting timeouts and failed embeddings. customer-impact channel: #cs-prod-impacted. labeling as "potential SLA" until mitigated.

Sam (sre): quick repro — `curl -X POST /v1/embeddings -d '{"input":"<long document>"}'` against canary returns 502/503 after ~600ms. stack shows `quant-kernel-select -> allocate_kv_cache -> segfault` on one node.

Olivia (oncall): good catch. if segfaulting kernel, we should divert canary traffic to previous stable model and rollback. requesting eng for emergency rollback.

Anna (eng): can do. recommended mitigations: 1) divert canary traffic to stable (`traffic-split set deploy-20260312-1145->0%`), 2) enqueue rollback for canary release, 3) disable the new kernel flag.

Sam (sre): executing diversion now: `./infra traffic-split set --id deploy-20260312-1145 --fraction 0`

deploy-bot: traffic-split command accepted; canary fraction -> 0%. routing now to stable pool (v2.13.3).

incident-bot: PagerDuty INC12345 status -> acknowledged by Olivia. escalations paused. notifying engineering rotation.

Olivia (oncall): issuing emergency rollback: `/deploy rollback deploy-20260312-1145 --scope canary --reason "5xx spike / kernel segfault"`

deploy-bot: rollback job started for deploy-20260312-1145. estimated 60-120s to drain and redeploy. job id rb-336777.

Sam (sre): monitoring metrics. 5xx count starting to drop on routing change. p95 falling. attaching quick grafana snapshots: `embed_gen/5xx_rate`, `embed_gen/p95_latency`.

Carter (support): notifying affected customers: initial message sent to 3 customers, advising workaround (retry after 1m) and that we're rolling back canary.

Anna (eng): disabling kernel flag in config repo: `git revert --no-ff f2b3a7e` then will push hotfix if rollback doesn't fully mitigate.

Sam (sre): after traffic diversion + rollback in progress: 5xx rate in canary subset down from 3.8% -> 0.4% in next 2 mins. stable pool unaffected. looks like immediate mitigation working.

Olivia (oncall): thanks. holding for 15m watch. if metrics stay stable, we'll resolve. Sam, can you drive the postmortem and capture deploy diff + reproducer? Anna to own fix.

Anna (eng): will open PR to remove kernel auto-switch and add stricter unit tests for long-sequence path. adding `@sam` to reviewer.

Sam (sre): creating incident ticket: INC12345-20260312 in backlog, summary: canary v2.14.0 triggered quant-kernel segfault -> 5xx surge. adding logs, traces, and commands used. assigning to Anna + SRE for RCA.

Carter (support): CS note: 3 impacted customers, none reported data loss, only transient timeouts. we queued follow-up emails. marking severity as P2 for now.

deploy-bot: rollback rb-336777 completed successfully. canary instances drained and replaced with stable version.

Sam (sre): metrics check: `embed-gen` 5xx back to baseline, p95 normalized to previous levels. will continue to monitor for 30m.

incident-bot: PagerDuty INC12345 -> resolved by Olivia (oncall). resolution note: traffic diverted + emergency rollback; root cause under investigation.

Olivia (oncall): resolving thread for now. handing to Sam/Anna for the full postmortem and timeline. I'll append incident timeline to the ticket. :white_check_mark:

Sam (sre): ack — will publish timeline + mitigation steps, include commands used and suggested observability tweaks (add canary-specific kv-cache tracing).

Anna (eng): will follow with PR and schedule a canary-only test run to reproduce long-input path. thanks all for fast responses. :thumbsup:

Carter (support): closing CS loop once postmortem has customer-facing blurb.

Olivia (oncall): last check-in: metrics green at 09:34 UTC. leaving watch for 20m then unassign. great teamwork.
